new_rules: R13: Support for a newly released version of a runtime, platform or peer dependency ("Support X n", a widened peer range, a compatibility bump) is actionable: the project can now upgrade that dependency. It is a capability, so benefit none (R6), and change_type other unless labelled a fix.

R14: A new or stricter type-checker or linter diagnostic or rule is actionable (code to fix, or a rule to configure or suppress). When it newly rejects or flags code the previous version accepted (reject, ban, diagnose, check, emit diagnostics), it is breaking, because the type check of unchanged code now fails. Benefit is none unless the record states it catches a bug (R6).

R15: In a type checker, support for or inference of a language or library construct it did not handle before changes the check results on existing code, so it is behavior_change: not fix unless labelled a fix, and not other. A change confined to IDE or LSP features is tooling. Benefit is none unless stated.
R16: A fix for a performance defect (memory leak, memory growth, slowness, low frame rate) gets correctness (R4) and performance (the memory or speed gain is the stated subject).

R17: A run-time change with no fix label (new handler wiring, gesture cancellation, callbacks now firing, changed ordering, implementing a protocol method, no longer taking over a delegate) is behavior_change with benefit none (R4 and R6). "By default" without a named existing option is behavior_change, not default_change.

R18: A change that is agreed breaking, or listed under breaking changes and needing project action, is not change_type fix even when it is described as a correction. It is behavior_change (this generalises R7).

R19: An API moved to a new location is removal and breaking when the source says to migrate and does not say the old location still works ("now lives in", "migrate"). It is deprecation when the move is advisory ("going forward", "rather than") and nothing says the old path fails.

R20: Type definitions added or corrected for an existing runtime option or feature (an option missing from an interface, exactOptionalPropertyTypes support, deep keyPrefix typing) are change_type fix (R5), benefit none, and not actionable. Typing enabled by a new opt-in option is new_option and actionable.
R21: Failing earlier or more clearly on input that was already invalid (an invariant instead of a later failure) is a diagnostic improvement, so benefit none (R3 and R6).
R22: Relaxing a requirement on the project (a CSP directive or permission no longer needed) is not breaking, because existing setups keep working. It is behavior_change, not removal.
R23: Something the project could previously do through an existing API that it can no longer do (an event callback that could supply a value and is now notify-only) is removal (R10).
